title: Add Health Check
summary: Adds liveness and readiness endpoints that test real dependencies with short timeouts, so orchestrators restart the right things.
description: A health route that always returns 200 hides outages, and one that calls every dependency on each probe can cause them. This command adds two separate checks: one that says the process is alive, and one that says it can do work.
Each dependency check has a hard timeout and runs a cheap query. The response names what failed without leaking connection strings or versions.
useWhen: Kubernetes, ECS or a load balancer needs probes
Deploys send traffic to instances that are not ready
Your current /health returns ok even when the database is down
You are adding a service and want monitoring hooks from day one
body:
Add health endpoints to this service. Dependencies to include: $ARGUMENTS (detect them from config if empty).

1. Read the app entry point, config and client setup to list real dependencies: database, cache, queue, object storage, upstream APIs.
2. Add `GET /livez`: returns 200 with no dependency calls. It only proves the process responds.
3. Add `GET /readyz`: runs one cheap check per required dependency in parallel (for example `SELECT 1`, a cache PING), each with a 1 to 2 second timeout. Return 200 when all pass, otherwise 503 with JSON like {"status":"degraded","failed":["database"]}.
4. Mark optional dependencies as non-fatal so a flaky analytics API does not take the service out of rotation.
5. Never include secrets, hostnames, stack traces or version numbers in the body. Skip auth on these routes but do not expose them publicly if the platform supports an internal port.
6. Reuse existing connections; do not open a new pool per probe.
7. Add tests for all-healthy and one-dependency-down, then run them. Show the probe snippet for the deploy config and ask before editing it.

example.result:
Added /livez (static 200) and /readyz (Postgres SELECT 1, Redis PING, 1.5s timeout each, run in parallel).
Down redis returns 503 {"status":"degraded","failed":["redis"]}. 3 tests pass.
Suggested probe: readiness path /readyz, period 10s, failureThreshold 3.

faq.question: Why two endpoints?
faq.answer: Liveness restarts a stuck process, readiness only removes it from traffic. Mixing them makes a database blip restart every instance.

faq.question: Could the checks slow the service down?
faq.answer: They are cheap queries on shared connections with short timeouts, and they run in parallel.

access: Reads app startup code and configuration
Edits source and test files, deploy config only after you agree
